justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: x-axis shows days 0–4 with evenly spaced tick positions (regular timecourse), so no discontinuity or break is indicated or needed.
y-axes show continuous numeric scales (different ranges per subplot) with regularly spaced tick marks and no abrupt numeric jumps; no visual break markers are present or required.

Flow cytometry scatter plots use continuous fluorescence intensity axes (log-scale decades typical) and quadrant percentages; tick marks/decades appear continuous with no skipped numeric ranges or visual break marks.
As above, y-axis shows continuous intensity scale with no abrupt jump in tick labeling or any break symbol; no axis break is present or necessary.
x-axis represents experimental conditions/concentration series (categorical positions) rather than a numeric axis with omitted ranges; spacing is categorical and no axis break marker is needed.
y-axis is percent (0–100) with regular tick spacing and no skipped values or discontinuity requiring a break marker.
x-axis uses discrete experimental condition positions (categorical/timepoints); there is no indication of an omitted numeric interval that would require a break marker.
y-axis percentage scale is continuous and regularly labeled; no abrupt numeric jumps or visual discontinuities are present.
x-axis indicates population identifiers / categories for boxplots; categorical axis spacing is appropriate and does not require a break marker.
y-axis (normalized read counts) shows continuous numeric scaling with regularly spaced ticks; no skipped ranges or visual discontinuities are present that would require an axis break.
Heatmap x-axis lists sample/population labels (categorical); there is no numeric axis with omitted ranges requiring a break marker.
Heatmap y-axis lists gene labels (categorical) and the data are represented by color scale rather than a numeric axis with omitted intervals; no axis break is required.
